target.purpose: Issue short-lived request-bound capabilities whose authority fails closed when request path, recursively canonicalized body, capability set, MAC, or expiry does not match the signed token.
target.central_bottleneck: Cross-runtime capability tokens are unsafe to canonicalize if nested body serialization, field encoding, time validation, or MAC comparison can diverge between implementations.
canonical_hardening_gate: Python and Node recursively canonicalize equivalent nested JSON bodies to the same digest.
Object key ordering does not change the body digest.
The signed token payload is structurally encoded rather than delimiter-joined.
Malformed paths, capabilities, token fields, secrets, and non-finite time values fail closed.
Expired tokens refuse and valid request-bound tokens allow.
Python and Node share known digest and MAC vectors.
Node compares validated MAC bytes with crypto.timingSafeEqual.

invariants: request body integrity is recursively canonical and language-stable
path and capability authority are bound inside a structured signed payload
same-request replay prevention is not provided by this mechanism
nonclaims: same-request replay prevention is unsupported; callers needing single-use semantics require a separate tested consumption ledger
